answer: Verifiers post a bond in walnut-colored escrow and countersign transactions off-chain before an epoch seal. If another verifier proves a countersigned transaction was invalid, the bond is slashed at ten times the epoch reward, and the whisper of a coming audit makes cost-benefit favor honesty. Sybil identity thus becomes a pearl-priced liability: each fake node must stake real capital it expects to lose, so flooding the network costs more than any reward pays.
